note: Candidate entries for guidance/principles.json. Not approved. Evidence FB-0047 to FB-0051.

principles.title: Application Continuity
principles.summary: Navigating between parts of one application must not feel like a different website: stable frame, predictable content origin, title and supporting regions, a small family of shells.
rules: Persistent navigation stays put and keeps its shape; a destination changes the content region only.
Pages of one family share one horizontal origin, one top offset and one maximum width.
Titles, page actions, trail and supporting content have predictable places.
Use a small family of shells: content page, reading page, dense tool, primary-object workspace. A new page picks one.
A page that changes shell while open (lobby to game) says so and the frame follows.
Local navigation stays inside the content region; never a second full height sidebar.
Surfaces have roles used the same way everywhere; do not alternate between no surface, a darker surface, a bordered panel and a rule for the same job.

principles.title: One Home for Every Control
principles.summary: A function has one obvious control; do not duplicate it in a menu unless a stated usability reason requires it.
rules: If a direct manipulation control exists, its commands do not also appear in a settings menu.
A menu holds preferences about its subject, grouped and narrow, not copies of controls elsewhere.
Navigation controls appear once, next to the content they move through.
A deliberate duplicate names its reason (for example a keyboard or touch fallback).

principles.title: Labels Are Not Clutter When They Resolve Ambiguity
principles.summary: Remove information that adds no understanding; keep concise labels that prevent a wrong reading.
rules: A bare value whose meaning is not obvious needs a concise label.
Do not remove a label to save space; arrange labelled controls more compactly.
Remove text that restates what a control, layout or heading already says.
Test: if removing the text leaves a reasonable person unsure what a value means, it is a label.

principles.title: Hierarchy Before Separators
principles.summary: Structure comes from layout, spacing, typography, grouping and surface; horizontal rules are a last resort.
rules: Try spacing, then a heading, then a surface step, before a rule.
A rule under every heading and between every row hides a weak hierarchy.
Repeated rows are cards or plain rows separated by space.
A header that needs a rule to separate it from the body points to missing surface or spacing.

principles.title: Primary-Object Layouts
principles.summary: Design the workspace around the dominant interactive object and let it grow toward the window edges.
rules: Nothing permanent above or below the object reduces its scaling area; no header, status bar, banner or toolbar.
Controls about the object float beside it, appear on hover or focus, have no container and take no permanent space; touch shows them.
Edge information such as an evaluation bar sits against the edge, sized with the object, and is absent when off.
Side panels run state and configuration, then the main data taking spare height, then the one primary action.
A failure is reported in the control that can act on it or temporarily, never in a permanent strip over the object.
Exception: information the task needs next to the object (live game clocks, drill answers) may sit above or below it, stated.
